package_info.package_versions: N/A (multiple variants targeting South Korean users)
package_info.why_malicious: The FakeCalls Android Trojan impersonates over 20 financial apps, simulates voice calls with fake bank employees, and exfiltrates private data from victims' devices. Its primary purpose is to deceive users into divulging sensitive information and to steal private data, constituting clear malicious intent.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user launches fake banking app or receives a call)
execution_context.file_location: Malicious APK main activity and supporting classes

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code displays a fake banking app interface, simulates a call with a fake bank employee using pre-recorded audio, records the user's responses, collects private data from the device, and exfiltrates all gathered information to a command-and-control server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app mimics legitimate financial applications and simulates phone calls to trick users into revealing sensitive information, while also harvesting and exfiltrating private data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate banking app should not simulate calls with fake employees, record user audio without consent, or exfiltrate private data to unknown servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may use audio for customer support or voice authentication, but always with explicit user consent and without exfiltrating data to untrusted servers.
key_indicators: Simulation of voice calls with pre-recorded audio
Unauthorized recording and exfiltration of user audio
Collection and exfiltration of private device data

attack_chain.action: User installs the FakeCalls APK, believing it to be a legitimate banking app.
attack_chain.leads_to: App is launched and begins malicious activity.

attack_chain.action: App presents a fake banking interface and prompts the user to initiate a call or responds to an incoming call event.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is engaged in a simulated conversation with a fake bank employee.

attack_chain.action: App plays pre-recorded audio to simulate a bank employee, records the user's responses, and collects private data from the device.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive information and private data are gathered.

attack_chain.action: App exfiltrates the recorded audio and collected data to a remote command-and-control server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen information for further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: Android app mimicking multiple financial institutions
Simulated voice calls with pre-recorded audio
Unauthorized audio recording during app use
Exfiltration of audio and private data to external servers
file_indicators: APK package names similar to legitimate South Korean banking apps but with minor deviations
Presence of pre-recorded audio files within the APK assets
Unusual permissions: microphone, contacts, call logs, network
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure associated with FakeCalls
Unusual data uploads during or after simulated calls
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android applications requesting excessive permissions (microphone, contacts, call logs) while mimicking financial institutions. Analyze app behavior for simulated calls using pre-recorded audio and check for unauthorized audio recording and exfiltration. Network monitoring should flag connections to known C2 domains or suspicious data uploads during app use.
